senses.title: A Concept: something known in the mind
senses.titleCN: 概念：心里认识到的东西
senses.definition: a general concept or conception formed in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成的一般概念或观念
senses.example: The notion of fairness varies from culture to culture.
senses.exampleCN: “公平”这一概念因文化而异。
senses.why: Latin notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea held in the mind, not a written note.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notio 是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名的是“认知动作的结果”，即心里持有的观念，而不是写下的“笔记”。

senses.title: A Picture in the Mind: a mental image
senses.definition: a mental image or impression of something, often only roughly defined
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的心理图像或印象，常常只有粗略的轮廓
senses.example: I had only a vague notion of the city before I arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 到达之前，我对这座城市只有一个模糊的印象。
senses.why: Knowing something can begin with a shape rather than a definition. The result of that knowing is a picture with soft edges, which English calls a notion.
senses.whyCN: 认识一件事可以从一个轮廓开始，而不是从定义开始。这种认识的结果是一幅边缘模糊的画面，英语就叫 notion。

senses.title: Awareness: having no notion of something
senses.definition: knowledge or awareness of something, chiefly in the phrase have no notion of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的了解或意识，主要用于 have no notion of 这一说法
senses.example: He had no notion of how much the repairs would cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他完全不知道修理要花多少钱。
senses.why: If notio is the result of knowing, then having no notion is having no result at all: the mind holds nothing on the matter.
senses.whyCN: 如果 notio 是认知的结果，那么 have no notion 就是完全没有结果：心里对这件事空无一物。

senses.title: An Opinion: a view held as true
senses.definition: an opinion or view, especially one held without full proof
senses.definitionCN: 观点或看法，尤指没有充分证据却仍持有的
senses.example: She rejected the old notion that children should be seen and not heard.
senses.exampleCN: 她否定了“孩子只该被看见、不该被听见”的旧观念。
senses.why: By c.1600 the concept in the mind was treated as a view about the world. The mental result now faces outward as an opinion someone holds.
senses.whyCN: 到 17 世纪早期，心里的概念被当作对世界的看法。这个心理结果转向外部，成了某人持有的观点。

senses.title: A Whim: an inclination with no deep reason
senses.titleCN: 念头：没有多少理由的兴之所至
senses.definition: a whimsical or not very rational inclination to do something
senses.definitionCN: 一时兴起、没有多少理性依据的做事倾向
senses.example: On a whim, he took the notion to paint the door blue.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时兴起，动了把门漆成蓝色的念头。
senses.why: A notion can be an idea that arrives without evidence or plan. From 1746 the word also names such a light, self-generated inclination, close to a whim.
senses.whyCN: notion 可以是一个没有证据、没有计划就冒出来的想法。自 1746 年起，这个词也指这种轻飘飘、自发产生的倾向，接近 whim。

senses.title: An Intention: have a notion to do
senses.definition: an intention or plan, chiefly in the phrase have a notion to do something
senses.definitionCN: 意图或打算，主要用于 「have a notion to do something」 这一说法
senses.example: She had a notion to visit the museum before it closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她打算在博物馆闭馆前去一趟。
senses.why: An inclination that survives long enough becomes an intention. The same mental result now points toward a future action rather than a mere picture.
senses.whyCN: 一种倾向如果持续得够久，就变成打算。同一个心理结果此刻指向未来的行动，而不只是一幅画面。

senses.title: A Vague Belief: I had a notion that
senses.definition: a belief or suspicion held without certainty, often introduced by I had a notion that
senses.definitionCN: 没有把握的信念或猜疑，常由 I had a notion that 引出
senses.example: I had a notion that the keys were still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我总觉得钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The mind's result may be uncertain but still acted on. A notion here is a belief with no firm evidence, the softest form of thinking something is true.
senses.whyCN: 心里的结果可以并不确定，却仍会影响行动。这里的 notion 是没有坚实证据的信念，是“认为某事为真”最柔软的形式。

senses.title: Notions: small goods on a counter
senses.definition: in American English, small useful articles such as thread, pins, and buttons sold in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指针线、别针、纽扣等在商店出售的小件用品
senses.example: The general store kept buttons and thread among its notions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家杂货店把纽扣和线归在小商品里。
senses.why: In 1803 American English used notions for small clever inventions, then for the small goods a dry-goods store sold. The 'bright idea' became a physical trinket.
senses.whyCN: 1803 年美式英语用 notions 指“聪明的小发明”，随后指干货店出售的小商品。“灵光一现的想法”变成了手里的实物小件。

senses.title: The Philosopher's Notion: Cicero's loan translation
senses.titleCN: 哲学家的概念：西塞罗的仿译
senses.definition: in philosophy, a general idea formed by abstraction, especially as Cicero translated Greek ennoia or prolepsis
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中通过抽象形成的一般观念，尤指西塞罗对希腊语 ennoia 或 prolepsis 的仿译
senses.example: The Stoics debated whether a notion could arise before any experience.
senses.exampleCN: 斯多葛派争论概念能否在任何经验之前产生。
senses.why: Cicero needed a Latin word for Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' and prolepsis 'previous notion'. He used notio, the result of noscere, to name an abstract idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗需要给希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”和 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”找拉丁词。他用了 notio，即 noscere 的结果，来命名心中的抽象观念。

intro.en: Notion comes from Latin notio, an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea in the mind, and Cicero used it to translate Greek philosophical terms.
intro.cn: notion 来自拉丁语 notio，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名认知动作的结果，即心中的观念；西塞罗曾用它翻译希腊哲学术语。

items.en: Recorded as nocioun, meaning 'a general concept, conception'.
items.cn: 以 nocioun 的形式记录，意为“一般概念、观念”。

items.en: From Latin notionem (nominative notio) 'concept, conception, idea, notice', an action noun from the past-participle stem of noscere 'come to know'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 notionem（主格 notio）“概念、观念、想法、知悉”，是 noscere“认识、得知”过去分词词干的动作名词。

items.en: Noscere traces to PIE *gno- 'to know', the same family that gives know and knowledge.
items.cn: noscere 可追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”，与英语 know、knowledge 同族。

items.en: Cicero formed notio as a loan translation of Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' or prolepsis 'previous notion'.
items.cn: 西塞罗用 notio 仿译希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”或 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”。

items.en: The sense 'opinion, view' is recorded; the modern word now covers both a concept and a stance.
items.cn: 记录到“意见、看法”义；现代这个词同时覆盖“概念”和“立场”。

items.en: The sense 'whim, not very rational inclination' appears in 1746, and American English notions 'small goods' in 1803, by way of 'clever little inventions'.
items.cn: 1746 年出现“念头、不太理性的倾向”义；1803 年美式英语出现 notions“小商品”义，经由“聪明的小发明”这一想法。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound; the second for overlapping meaning, so form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义重叠挑选，使词形与词义分开。

entries.definition: attention or a written announcement. It comes from Latin notitia 'knowledge', a close relative of notio, not from notion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 注意；书面通知。它来自拉丁语 notitia“知悉”，是 notio 的近亲，而不是 notion 的派生词。

entries.definition: a country and its people. It looks close to notion but comes from Latin natio 'birth, race', with no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 国家与国民。它拼写像 notion，但来自拉丁语 natio“出生、族类”，没有共同词根。

entries.definition: a system of written symbols. It comes from Latin nota 'mark', a different branch from notio.
entries.definitionCN: 符号体系。它来自拉丁语 nota“记号”，与 notio 是不同分支。

entries.definition: the broadest word for something in the mind. Notion is narrower and often suggests something vague or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“心中所想”最宽泛的词。notion 更窄，常暗示模糊或个人的成分。

entries.definition: a general idea formed by abstraction. It is more formal and precise than notion.
entries.definitionCN: 通过抽象形成的一般观念。它比 notion 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: acceptance that something is true. It is stronger than a notion, which may be little more than a hunch.
entries.definitionCN: 接受某事为真。它比 notion 更强，notion 可能只是一种直觉。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: notio is the result of noscere 'to know', and English notice, notify and notorious belong to the same knowing family.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：notio 是 noscere“知道”的结果，英语 notice、notify、notorious 都属于同一个“认知”词族。

normal.en: Notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know': it is the result of knowing, not a written note.
normal.cn: notio 是 noscere“认识”的动作名词：它是认知的结果，不是写下的笔记。

normal.en: Notice, notify and notorious all go back to the same 'know' root, so the not- in notion is a knowing not-.
normal.cn: notice、notify、notorious 都回到同一个“知道”词根，所以 notion 里的 not- 是“认知”的 not-。

normal.en: Have no notion of means the mind holds nothing at all on the subject.
normal.cn: have no notion of 意思是心里对这件事空无一物。

normal.en: A vague notion is an idea whose edges have not been drawn yet.
normal.cn: a vague notion 是边缘还没画清楚的观念。

normal.en: Notions on a shop counter are small goods, a sense that grew out of 'clever little inventions'.
normal.cn: 柜台上的 notions 是小商品，这个义项从“聪明的小发明”长出来。

abstract.en: Picture a shape forming in mist: you can point at it, but you cannot trace its outline.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中渐渐成形的轮廓：你能指向它，却描不出边界。

abstract.en: The same shape can harden into an opinion or soften into a whim.
abstract.cn: 同一团轮廓可以硬化成观点，也可以软化成一时兴起。

abstract.en: Follow it into a shop and it shrinks to a button on a notions counter.
abstract.cn: 跟着它走进商店，它就缩成小商品柜台上一枚纽扣。

examples.en: He had no notion of how difficult the language would be.
examples.cn: 他完全不知道这门语言会有多难。

examples.en: The notion that money brings happiness is widely questioned.
examples.cn: “金钱带来幸福”这一观念受到广泛质疑。

examples.en: The old shop sold needles, ribbons, and other notions.
examples.cn: 那家老店出售针、缎带和其他小商品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺神」——脑子里“诺”的一声，仿佛神仙递来一个模糊念头 → notion 概念、想法

root: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词，追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”；notio 是认知动作的结果，不是“笔记”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of notion all name something the mind knows. The knowing can be a concept, a picture, an opinion, a whim, an intention, a hunch, a shop-counter trinket, or a philosopher's abstraction.
sensesIntro.cn: notion 的九个义项都在命名“心里知道的东西”。这种知道可以是概念、画面、看法、一时兴起、打算、直觉、柜台小商品，或哲学家的抽象观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape forming in the mind, known before it is clearly defined.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中渐渐成形的轮廓，先被知道，后才有清楚定义。

branches.en: THE KNOWN SHAPE: a general concept, and a mental picture with soft edges.
branches.cn: 被认知的轮廓：一般概念，以及边缘模糊的心理画面。

branches.en: AWARENESS: having a notion, or having no notion at all.
branches.cn: 知晓：有概念，或完全没有概念。

branches.en: VIEW AND BELIEF: an opinion held as true, and a hunch held without certainty.
branches.cn: 看法与信念：自认为真的观点，以及没有把握的直觉。

branches.en: INCLINATION AND INTENTION: a whim that arrives, and a plan that stays.
branches.cn: 倾向与意图：突然到来的念头，以及留下来成为打算的念头。

branches.en: FROM TRINKET TO ABSTRACTION: small shop goods, and Cicero's philosophical concept.
branches.cn: 从小商品到抽象：柜台小货，以及西塞罗的哲学概念。

intro.en: Notion is the Latin noun notio in English form. Its family adds -al, -ly and -ity, while notice, notify and notorious belong to the same noscere 'know' root.
intro.cn: notion 是拉丁语名词 notio 的英语形式。它的词族加 -al、-ly、-ity，而 notice、notify、notorious 属于同一个 noscere“知道”词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin notio 'concept, idea' is an action noun from noscere 'come to know', whose participle notus 'known' also underlies notice and notify. The deepest root is PIE *gno- 'to know'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”是 noscere“认识”的动作名词；其分词 notus“已知的”也支撑着 notice 与 notify。最深层词根是原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”。

items.meaning: a concept or idea in the mind
items.meaningCN: 心中的概念或想法（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The notion of progress is not universal.
items.exampleCN: “进步”这一观念并非普世皆同。

items.meaningCN: 概念上的；理论上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The cost is notional until the contract is signed.
items.exampleCN: 合同签订前，这项费用只是名义上的。

items.meaningCN: 概念上；名义上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two departments are notionally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个部门名义上是分开的。

items.meaningCN: 概念性（-ity 构成名词，哲学用语）
items.example: The paper questions the notionality of pure sense data.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文质疑纯粹感觉材料的概念性。

items.meaning: small useful goods sold in a shop
items.meaningCN: 小商品；杂货（复数形式，美式英语）
items.example: She bought thread and buttons at the notions counter.
items.exampleCN: 她在小商品柜台买了线和纽扣。

items.meaningCN: 注意；通知（同出 notus“已知的”）
items.example: A notice was posted on the door.

items.meaning: to make someone know; to inform
items.meaningCN: 通知；告知（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: Please notify the office of any change.
items.exampleCN: 如有变动，请通知办公室。

items.meaningCN: 通知；告示（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The app sends a notification when the file is ready.
items.exampleCN: 文件准备好时，应用会发出通知。

items.meaning: well known, usually for something bad
items.meaningCN: 臭名昭著的；众所周知的（-orious 构成形容词）
items.example: The road is notorious for winter accidents.
items.exampleCN: 这条路因冬季事故频发而臭名昭著。

latinEntries.meaning: to come to know, learn, recognize

definition_zh: 滋养；养育；培养；助长
definition_en: to give a person, animal or plant the food and care needed to grow, and to help an idea or feeling develop
core_image: 一只手把热汤稳稳送到嘴边，身体一点点有了力气
scene: 灶上的小火煨着一锅汤，母亲把勺子吹凉，再送到孩子嘴边，看着他慢慢有了血色。Warm soup and steady care nourished the boy through a long winter.
sceneCN: 这里 nourish 是「滋养、养育」（第 1 个义项：供给养分让身体长起来）；句意为热汤与悉心照料让男孩熬过了漫长的冬天。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、勺子、灶火。

derivatives.zh: 由 nourish 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「营养；食物」
由 nourish 加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「有营养的」
由表示「坏」的前缀 mal- 加 nourished 构成，义为「营养不良的」

senses.title: To give what the body needs for health
senses.definition: to provide a living thing with the food and substances it needs to stay healthy
senses.definitionCN: 给生物提供维持健康所需的食物与养分
senses.example: A balanced diet nourishes both body and brain.
senses.exampleCN: 均衡的饮食滋养身体和头脑。
senses.why: Latin nutrire meant to suckle and to feed, so the physical act of putting food into a body sits at the very centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养，所以「把食物送进身体」这个动作一直处在这个词的正中央。

senses.title: To feed and bring up a young person or animal
senses.definition: to care for a young person or animal until it can live on its own
senses.definitionCN: 照料幼小的生命，直到它能独立生活
senses.example: Her grandmother nourished her through a sickly childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把她这个体弱的孩子一手养大。
senses.why: Feeding a child is a single meal repeated day after day, so the same verb stretches from one serving of food to the whole work of raising someone.
senses.whyCN: 喂养孩子是一顿饭重复一天又一天，同一个动词便从「添一份饭」拉长成「把一个人养大」的全部工作。

senses.title: To help an idea or feeling grow
senses.definition: to keep a hope, feeling or relationship alive and growing
senses.definitionCN: 让希望、情感或关系保持活力并继续生长
senses.example: He nourished the hope of returning home one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他心里一直养着有一天回家的希望。
senses.why: An idea also needs to be fed; English borrows the bodily image and lets hopes and feelings be nourished as if they were living things.
senses.whyCN: 想法也需要被喂；英语借来身体层面的画面，让希望与情感像活物一样被滋养。

intro.en: Nourish goes back to a Latin verb for suckling and feeding, reached English through French, and now feeds bodies, soil, hopes and relationships alike.
intro.cn: nourish 可追溯到表示哺乳与喂养的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语，如今既喂养身体，也养护土壤、希望与关系。

items.en: Nutrire meant to suckle, to feed and to foster, already covering both the body and the person being raised.
items.cn: nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养、抚育，本已同时涵盖身体与被养大的人。

items.en: Nutrimentum named food and whatever feeds, and it stands behind the English words for nourishment.
items.cn: nutrimentum 指食物与养料，是英语中那组「营养」词汇的来源。

items.en: Old French nourrir meant to feed and to bring up, and it softened the Latin consonants on its way to English.
items.cn: 古法语 nourrir 意为喂养、抚育，在传入英语时软化了拉丁语的辅音。

items.en: Middle English nouren and nourishen kept both the feeding sense and the raising sense side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语的 nouren 与 nourishen 把喂养与抚养两层意思并排保留下来。

items.en: Modern English extends nourish to soil, skin, hopes and relationships, wherever something has to be kept alive.
items.cn: 现代英语把 nourish 扩展到土壤、皮肤、希望与关系，凡是需要维持生命的地方都能用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on this verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs for feeding and supporting growth.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个动词构成的同族词；近义组收表示喂养与扶持成长的动词。

entries.definition: Food or whatever is needed for growth and health.
entries.definitionCN: 食物，或成长与健康所需的一切。

entries.definition: Badly fed, so that the body lacks what it needs.
entries.definitionCN: 吃得很糟、身体缺少所需养分的。

entries.definition: Not given enough food over a long period.
entries.definitionCN: 长期得不到足够食物的。

entries.definition: To give food to a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 给人和动物食物。

entries.definition: To care for and encourage the growth of someone.
entries.definitionCN: 照料并鼓励某人成长。

entries.definition: To keep something alive or going over time.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物存活或持续。

entries.definition: To help something develop gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某事物逐渐发展。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from milk and warmth, and everything it later feeds, from soil to a hope, is treated as something that must be kept alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从奶与温度开始，后来它所喂养的一切，从土壤到一个希望，都被当作必须维持生命的东西。

normal.en: Nutrire in Latin meant to suckle and feed, so nourish begins with milk and warmth rather than with abstract care.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养，所以 nourish 的起点是奶与温度，而不是抽象的关心。

normal.en: Nourishment adds -ment to the verb and names what feeds, while the verb names the act of feeding.
normal.cn: nourishment 在动词后加 -ment，指「喂养的东西」，动词则指喂养这个动作。

normal.en: Malnourished puts mal-, bad, in front of nourished, so the body has been fed badly.
normal.cn: malnourished 在 nourished 前加表示「坏」的 mal-，指身体被喂得很糟。

normal.en: The same word feeds the body and feeds a hope, because English treats both as things that must be kept alive.
normal.cn: 同一个词既喂养身体，也滋养希望，因为英语把两者都当作必须维持生命的东西。

normal.en: Nourishing food is the plainest pairing, and the -ing form works directly as an adjective for whatever gives strength.
normal.cn: nourishing food 是最朴素的搭配，-ing 形式直接当形容词，指供给力气的东西。

abstract.en: A spoon held steady at a child's lips is the oldest picture of care that this word keeps.
abstract.cn: 一勺汤稳稳送到孩子嘴边，是这个词保存下来的最古老的照料画面。

abstract.en: What feeds the body and what feeds a hope obey one rule: something has to arrive regularly or the thing withers.
abstract.cn: 养身体的东西与养希望的东西遵守同一条规则：得定期送到，否则就会枯掉。

abstract.en: Nourish is a reminder that growing is not an event but a long series of small deliveries.
abstract.cn: nourish 提醒人：成长不是一件事，而是一长串小小的送达。

examples.en: A balanced diet nourishes both body and brain.
examples.cn: 均衡的饮食滋养身体和头脑。

examples.en: Her grandmother nourished her through a sickly childhood.
examples.cn: 祖母把她这个体弱的孩子一手养大。

examples.en: He nourished the hope of returning home one day.
examples.cn: 他心里一直养着有一天回家的希望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那瑞须」——那碗热汤里的细须，一口口把人养起来；nourish 就是滋养。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 nutrire（喂养、哺乳），经古法语 nourrir 进入英语；同族词多与「喂养、营养」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is feeding a living thing until it grows; the senses split between the body that is fed, the young that are raised, and the hopes and feelings that are kept alive the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把食物喂给一个活物，让它长起来；义项分出三处：被喂养的身体、被养大的幼者，以及用同样方式维持着的希望与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a warm spoon steady at someone's lips while strength slowly returns.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把温热的勺子稳稳停在嘴边，力气一点点回到身上。

branches.en: a bowl of soup set down in front of a tired child
branches.cn: 一碗汤放在疲倦的孩子面前

branches.en: soil given compost before the planting season
branches.cn: 播种前施了堆肥的土

branches.en: a grandmother feeding a frail girl year after year
branches.cn: 祖母年复一年喂着瘦弱的小姑娘

branches.en: a hope kept alive through long waiting
branches.cn: 在漫长等待里被养着的希望

branches.en: the same steady feeding given to a body and to a dream
branches.cn: 同样稳定的喂养，一份给身体，一份给梦想

intro.en: The word carries a Latin verb of feeding plus two English suffixes that turn it into a thing and a quality, with the negative prefix marking the failure of that feeding.
intro.cn: 这个词带着表示喂养的拉丁动词，再加两个英语后缀，把它变成「物」与「性质」，否定前缀则标出喂养的失败。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: means or result of an act

definition_zh: 小说；长篇小说；新奇的；新颖的；新颁律令（罕用）
definition_en: a long written story about imaginary people and events; also new and unlike anything seen before
core_image: 一本摊开的长篇手稿，纸页很新，故事却是从未有人讲过的
scene: 清晨的旧书店里，店主把一本厚厚的故事书摆到最显眼的位置。She borrowed a novel from the library and read it in two nights.
sceneCN: 这里是「小说、长篇小说」（第 1 个义项：虚构的长篇故事）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本小说，两个晚上就读完了。场景里可辨的物件：旧书架、厚书、昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 novel 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小说家」
由 novel 加名词后缀 -ty 构成，义为「新奇；新鲜事」
由 novelist 加 -ic 构成，义为「小说式的；具有小说特点的」

senses.title: A long work of fiction
senses.definition: a long written story in which the events and characters are imagined rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 篇幅较长、情节与人物皆为虚构的书面故事
senses.example: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。
senses.why: The noun entered English from Italian novella, a short tale, and later grew to mean a full-length invented story.
senses.whyCN: 名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）进入英语，后来指篇幅完整的虚构故事；它和形容词「新」共用同一拉丁词根，因为故事讲的正是没见过的事。

senses.title: New and unlike what came before
senses.definition: new, original and not seen or done before
senses.definitionCN: 新的、独创的、此前未曾见过或做过的
senses.example: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。
senses.why: The adjective goes back to Latin novellus, a small form of novus meaning new, so freshness is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可追到拉丁语 novellus，它是 novus（新的）的小称形式，所以「新鲜」才是这个词最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: A newly issued decree
senses.definition: a new decree or supplementary constitution, especially in civil law
senses.definitionCN: 尤指民法中新增的法令或补充律令，现代英语已罕用
senses.example: The old code was amended by a series of novels.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法典经一系列新颁律令得到修订。
senses.why: In civil law the plural novels named the new constitutions added after the main code, keeping the bare sense of something newly issued.
senses.whyCN: 在民法传统里，复数形式 novels 指编入主法典之后的新律令，保留了「新颁之物」的字面意思；这个义项今天基本只出现在法律史里。

intro.en: Novel runs on two rails from the same Latin root: an adjective for what is new, and a noun for an invented story that was itself a novelty.
intro.cn: novel 沿着同一拉丁词根分出两条路：形容词指「新的」，名词指虚构故事，而这类故事在当时本身就是新鲜事物。

items.en: Novus meant new, fresh or recent, and it stands behind a large family of words about novelty.
items.cn: novus 意为新的、新鲜的、刚出现的，是表示「新」的一大族词的共同词根。

items.en: Novellus was a diminutive of novus, literally newish or young, and it passed into several Romance languages.
items.cn: novellus 是 novus 的小称，字面意思是「较新的、年轻的」，它进入了多种罗曼语。

items.en: Old French novel meant new or fresh, and English took the adjective with that plain sense.
items.cn: 古法语 novel 意为新的、新鲜的，英语借入的形容词就带着这层朴素的意思。

items.en: Italian novella named a short tale, and through French nouvelle it gave English the noun for a story.
items.cn: 意大利语 novella 指短篇故事，经法语 nouvelle 传给英语，成为表示「故事」的名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective novel for anything strikingly new and the noun novel for a full-length fictional work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词 novel 指「格外新的」，名词 novel 则指篇幅完整的虚构作品。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group collects words for stories and for newness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示故事与「新」的词。

entries.definition: A short novel or a long short story.
entries.definitionCN: 篇幅较短的小说，或较长的短篇故事。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new thing.
entries.definitionCN: 新奇的性质，或新奇的小物件。

entries.definition: A person who writes novels.
entries.definitionCN: 写小说的人；小说家。

entries.definition: To introduce new ideas or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 引入新想法或新方法。

entries.definition: A person who is new to an activity or field.
entries.definitionCN: 刚接触某项活动或领域的新手。

entries.definition: Stories and characters that are invented rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的故事与人物，而非真人真事。

entries.definition: An account of events, whether real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的叙述，真实的或想象的。

entries.definition: New in design and not copied from anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 设计上新的，不是照搬别处的。

entries.definition: Recently made, arrived or thought of, and therefore new.
entries.definitionCN: 刚做出、刚到达或刚想到的，因而显得新。

normalIntro.en: The root nov means new, and from it grow the novel, the novelty and the person who writes novels.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 nov 表示「新」，小说、新奇与写小说的人都从它长出来。

normal.en: The Latin root nov means new, which is why a novel idea is simply a new idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 nov 表示「新」，所以 a novel idea 就是一个新想法。

normal.en: Novelty adds -ty to the same stem and turns new into a noun: the state of being new.
normal.cn: novelty 在同一词干后加 -ty，把「新」变成名词，指「新奇」这种状态。

normal.en: Novelist adds -ist, the suffix for a person, so it names the one who writes a novel.
normal.cn: novelist 加的是表示人的后缀 -ist，因此指写小说的人。

normal.en: Italian novella, a short tale, is the ancestor of the noun, which is why the two senses look unrelated.
normal.cn: 意大利语 novella 意为短篇故事，是名词义的祖先，所以两个义项看起来像是毫无关系。

normal.en: The adjective takes more novel and most novel, not noveler, because it is a longer adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词的比较级说 more novel、most novel，而不是 noveler，因为它属于较长的形容词。

abstract.en: A story and a new thing share one root because every story is, in a small way, something that did not exist before.
abstract.cn: 故事和新事物共用一个词根，因为每个故事在某种意义上都是过去不存在的东西。

abstract.en: Reading a novel means being handed a world that someone invented, so freshness lives inside the fictional sense too.
abstract.cn: 读一本小说，就是接过一个别人造出来的世界，所以「新」也活在虚构的那个义项里。

abstract.en: The word keeps two doors open: one leads to invention and one to novelty, and both open on the same Latin room.
abstract.cn: 这个词留着两扇门：一扇通向虚构，一扇通向新奇，而它们开在同一间拉丁语的屋子里。

examples.en: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。

examples.en: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
examples.cn: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。

examples.en: He writes novels about life in small mountain villages.
examples.cn: 他写关于山区小村生活的小说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹窝」——书里的故事闹成一窝，让人读到深夜；记住 novel 是小说。

root: 拉丁语 novus（新的）→ 小称 novellus（较新的）→ 形容词经古法语 novel 进入英语；名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）与法语 nouvelle 而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the Latin root for new; one branch names an invented long story, another describes anything strikingly fresh, and a third survives only in legal history.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是拉丁语表示「新」的词根；一条分支指虚构的长篇故事，一条形容格外新鲜的事物，第三条只留在法律史里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly written manuscript holding a story that nobody has told before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚写就的手稿，里面装着无人讲过的故事。

branches.en: a thick book left open on a night table
branches.cn: 床头摊开的一本厚书

branches.en: a reader refusing to close the last page
branches.cn: 读者舍不得合上最后一页

branches.en: a designer sketching a route no map has shown
branches.cn: 设计师画出一条地图上没有的路线

branches.en: a crowd hearing a proposal that breaks the old pattern
branches.cn: 众人听到一个打破旧套的方案

branches.en: a clerk copying a new decree into the law book
branches.cn: 书记员把新律令抄进法典

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin root for new, its adjective and its small form, plus two English suffixes that build the writer and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「新」的拉丁词根、它的形容词与小称之上，再由两个英语后缀造出「写的人」与「新的性质」。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus and its small form novellus supply the whole family, from the adjective novel to the noun novelty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 及其小称 novellus 支撑起整族词，从形容词 novel 到名词 novelty。

senses.definitionCN: 在我们正生活的当下这个时期
senses.example: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。
senses.why: The phrase behind the word literally meant now on days, so its first job is simply to place an action in the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的短语字面上就是「如今在这些日子里」，所以它最基本的工作是把动作安放在当下。

senses.title: The present seen against the past
senses.definition: used to point out how things differ between the present and an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出现在与从前之间的差别
senses.example: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。
senses.why: Because the phrase grew out of a comparison between days, the word naturally carries a before-and-after frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语本就诞生于「日子与日子」的对照，所以这个词天然带着「前后之别」的框架。

senses.title: Of the present period, placed before a noun
senses.titleCN: 时下的；当今的（口语用法）
senses.definition: placed before a noun in informal speech to mean belonging to the present period
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在名词前，表示属于当下这个时期的
senses.example: Nowadays children learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
senses.exampleCN: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。
senses.why: Once the adverb is felt as a label for the current era, speakers begin to use it as a modifier of the people and things that belong to that era.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被当成「当下时代」的标签，说话人就开始把它放到名词前，修饰属于这个时代的人与物。

intro.en: Nowadays began as a spoken phrase rather than a single word: now on days, which English later squeezed into one adverb.
intro.cn: nowadays 起初是一个口语短语而不是单词：now on days，后来英语把它压缩成一个副词。

items.en: The two halves are old: nu meant now, and dæg meant day.
items.cn: 两半都很古老：nu 意为「现在」，dæg 意为「日子」。

items.en: Middle English joined them in the phrase now a dayes, literally now on days, with a as a worn-down form of on.
items.cn: 中古英语把它们连成 now a dayes，字面是「如今在这些日子里」，其中的 a 是 on 的弱化形式。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the phrase was written as one word, and the old preposition had disappeared from hearing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个短语被写成一个词，旧的介词在听感上已经消失。

items.en: Dictionaries of the eighteenth century list it as a settled adverb of present time.
items.cn: 十八世纪的词典已把它收作表示现在时间的固定副词。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly in writing and in contrastive statements about how things have changed.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在书面语里、以及在说明事物如何变化的今昔对比句中使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short time words built from the same demonstrative parts; the near-meaning group collects other ways of saying now.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批指示词构成的短小时间词，近义组收其他表示「现在」的说法。

entries.definition: At this moment or at the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 此刻或现在。

entries.definition: On this present day.
entries.definitionCN: 在今天这一天。

entries.definition: In or to no place.
entries.definitionCN: 不在任何地方；无处。

entries.definition: Sometimes, but not often.
entries.definitionCN: 有时，但不常。

entries.definition: At the present time, common in neutral and formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 目前，常见于中性或正式书面语。

entries.definition: In the present period, especially in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在当前这段时期，多用于口语。

entries.definition: At this time, or soon, depending on the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 现时，或视句子指「不久」。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into now, a and dayes and it says now on these days, which is simply the present.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 now、a、dayes 三段，意思就是「在这些日子里」，也就是现在。

normal.en: Nowadays hides the words now and day inside it, and together they mean now on these days.
normal.cn: nowadays 里藏着 now 与 day，合起来就是「如今在这些日子里」。

normal.en: The a in the middle is a worn-down on, so the phrase once read as now on days.
normal.cn: 中间那个 a 是弱化掉的 on，所以这个短语原本读作 now on days。

normal.en: The final -s is the plural of day, which is why the word points to a stretch of days rather than one date.
normal.cn: 末尾的 -s 是 day 的复数，所以这个词指的是一段日子，而不是某一天。

normal.en: Nowadays is an adverb, so in careful writing it modifies a whole clause rather than standing before a noun.
normal.cn: nowadays 是副词，在严谨的写作里它修饰整个句子，而不是站在名词前面。

normal.en: Its closest short synonym in speech is these days, which carries the same contrast with the past.
normal.cn: 口语里它最贴近的短说法是 these days，同样带着与过去对照的意味。

abstract.en: The word is a fossil of a phrase: a whole remark about days was squeezed until it fit into one slot.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个短语的化石：一句关于日子的话被压缩到只占一个位置。

abstract.en: Hearing nowadays always implies a before, because a contrast with the past is built into its bones.
abstract.cn: 听到 nowadays 总会预设一个「从前」，因为与过去的对照已经长在它的骨架里。

abstract.en: It measures time the way a photograph does: it does not give the clock, only the fact that the picture has changed.
abstract.cn: 它衡量时间的方式像一张照片：它不报钟点，只说明画面已经变了。

examples.en: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
examples.cn: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。

examples.en: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
examples.cn: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。

examples.en: Children nowadays learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
examples.cn: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹啊得死」——如今的日子闹得人直喊要死；记住 nowadays 是现今。

root: 由 now（现在）、a（即 on）、day 的复数 dayes 合成的短语 now a dayes，十六世纪写成一个词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is present time; the senses divide into plain time reference, contrast with the past, and an informal attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「当下的时间」；义项分成单纯的时间定位、与从前的对照，以及口语里放在名词前的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old photograph and a new one of the same street, side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条街的旧照与新照并排摆着。

branches.en: a phone in every hand on a morning train
branches.cn: 早晨地铁里人人手中的手机

branches.en: a shop staying open late because customers now order at night
branches.cn: 因为客人改在夜里下单而开到很晚的店

branches.en: an old photograph held beside the same street today
branches.cn: 旧照片与今天的同一条街并排

branches.en: a grandmother still walking to the market
branches.cn: 仍然走去菜市场的祖母

branches.en: children swiping a screen before they can write
branches.cn: 还没会写字就先会滑屏幕的孩子

intro.en: The word is a fusion of now, a reduced on, and the plural of day; there is no Latin root, only old words that point at time.
intro.cn: 这个词由 now、弱化的 on 与 day 的复数三块拼成，没有拉丁词根，靠指示时间的旧词组成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 介词 on 的弱化形式

definition_zh: 无处；没有地方；毫无进展；偏远之地；远不及
definition_en: in or to no place at all; also used of a remote place and of a complete lack of progress
core_image: 一张地图上所有道路都走到尽头，前方再没有可以落脚的地方
scene: 夜里车在荒原上抛了锚，四周只有风声和黑黢黢的草。After two hours of walking, they found themselves nowhere near the village.
sceneCN: 这里是「远不及、离……还很远」（第 4 个义项：nowhere near 表示差得很远）；句意为走了两个小时，他们离村子还远得很。荒原与抛锚的车把「没有地方」的字面感先立了起来。

pos.zh: 偏远的地方（多见于 the middle of nowhere）

derivatives.zh: 由 nowhere 与 -ville 拼合的口语造词，指偏远又乏味的地方
由 nowhere 与 near 构成的固定搭配，义为「远不及」

senses.title: In or to no place
senses.definition: in or to no place at all
senses.definitionCN: 在任何地方都不存在，或不到任何地方
senses.example: The keys were nowhere in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。
senses.why: The word simply fused no with where, so it negates place itself: no location answers the question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是把 no 与 where 直接焊在一起，否定的是地点本身：没有任何一个位置能回答「在哪里」。

senses.title: To make no progress
senses.definition: to fail to make any progress or reach any result
senses.definitionCN: 没能取得任何进展或结果
senses.example: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 和他争辩毫无用处。
senses.why: If the destination is no place, movement toward it can only end without arrival, which is how the word came to mean no result.
senses.whyCN: 既然目的地是「没有地方」，朝它走就永远到不了，于是这个词引申为「没有结果」。

senses.title: A remote and empty place
senses.definition: a place far from towns and hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 远离城镇、难以抵达的地方
senses.example: They built a cabin in the middle of nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在荒郊野外盖了一间小木屋。
senses.why: When a location is so far out that it feels like no place at all, the negated word becomes a name for remoteness itself.
senses.whyCN: 当某个地方远得像是「根本不存在」时，这个否定词就反过来成了「偏远」的代称。

senses.title: Far from reaching a standard
senses.definition: used before near or close to say that something is far from a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在 near 或 close 前，表示离目标差得很远
senses.example: The project is nowhere near finished.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目离完工还差得远。
senses.why: The same spatial gap that produced no place is reused as a gap in degree, so distance in space turns into distance from a standard.
senses.whyCN: 造出「没有地方」的那个空间落差被挪来表示程度差距：空间的距离变成了与标准的距离。

intro.en: Nowhere is a compound of two Old English words, na and hwaer, and it has kept its literal shape for centuries.
intro.cn: nowhere 由两个古英语词 na 与 hwaer 复合而成，几个世纪以来一直保持着字面的构造。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not any.
items.cn: na 是朴素的否定词，意为「没有、一点也不」。

items.en: Hwaer was the question word for place, the ancestor of where.
items.cn: hwaer 是询问地点的疑问词，是 where 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the compound as nawher or nowher, still spelling out both halves.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个复合词写作 nawher 或 nowher，两半仍看得清楚。

items.en: Early modern printers settled on nowhere, and the word also began to name remote places.
items.cn: 近代早期的印刷者把拼写固定为 nowhere，这个词也开始用来指偏远之地。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative senses of no result and far from a standard, as in get nowhere and nowhere near.
items.cn: 现代英语再加上「没有结果」与「远不及」两个比喻义，如 get nowhere 与 nowhere near。

note.en: The look-alike group collects place adverbs built on where; the near-meaning group collects words for remoteness and for useless effort.
note.cn: 形近组收由 where 构成的同族地点副词，近义组收表示偏远与徒劳的词。

entries.definition: In or to a place that is not named.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到某个未指明的地方。

entries.definition: In or to any place at all.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何地方。

entries.definition: In or to all places.
entries.definitionCN: 到处；各处。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到别处。

entries.definition: Far away from towns and people.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇与人群的。

entries.definition: Cut off from others and hard to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 与外界隔绝、难以抵达的。

entries.definition: In a way that produces no result.
entries.definitionCN: 以毫无结果的方式。

entries.definition: A wild area with no towns or roads.
entries.definitionCN: 没有城镇与道路的荒野。

normalIntro.en: No plus where spells out no place; from that blank the word grows the senses of no result and far from a mark.
normalIntro.cn: no 与 where 一拼就写出「没有地方」；从这个空白里又长出「没有结果」与「差得远」。

normal.en: Nowhere is no plus where, so its literal meaning is not any place.
normal.cn: nowhere 就是 no 加 where，字面意思是不在任何地方。

normal.en: Because the destination is no place, get nowhere means you never arrive at a result.
normal.cn: 因为终点就是「没有地方」，所以 get nowhere 指永远到不了结果。

normal.en: Nowhere near keeps the same gap but measures distance from a target, not from a town.
normal.cn: nowhere near 保留同一个落差，只是量的是与目标的距离，而不是与城镇的距离。

normal.en: The middle of nowhere turns the negative into a name for the emptiest place around.
normal.cn: the middle of nowhere 把这个否定词反过来当成最空旷之处的名字。

normal.en: Spell it as one word: there is no space between no and where.
normal.cn: 拼写时写成一个词，no 与 where 之间不留空格。

abstract.en: A road ends in open grass: every direction has been walked and none leads anywhere.
abstract.cn: 一条路在荒草里到头：每个方向都走过了，哪儿也去不了。

abstract.en: Nowhere is the map's way of drawing an absence, a blank where a name should be.
abstract.cn: nowhere 是地图画「空缺」的方式：本该写名字的地方留了一片空白。

abstract.en: The same word can lose a place and lose a result, because both are destinations that never arrive.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能失去地点，也能失去结果，因为两者都是永远抵达不了的终点。

examples.en: The keys were nowhere in the room.
examples.cn: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。

examples.en: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
examples.cn: 和他争辩毫无用处。

examples.en: The project is nowhere near finished.
examples.cn: 这个项目离完工还差得远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹胃」——找不到地方吃饭，胃里闹得慌；记住 nowhere 是无处。

root: 古英语 na（不）与 hwær（何处）复合，字面即「何处都没有」；同族词为 somewhere、anywhere、everywhere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the absence of a place; the senses move from literal no place to no progress, a remote spot, and a gap in degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有地点」；义项先落在空间上的无处，再引申为没有进展、偏远之地，以及程度上的远不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that runs out at the edge of open grass, with no name on the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在荒草边缘走到尽头，地图上也没有名字。

branches.en: keys missing from every drawer in the room
branches.cn: 钥匙翻遍房间每个抽屉都不见

branches.en: a map with a blank space where a village should be
branches.cn: 本该标着村庄的地图却是一片空白

branches.en: two people arguing until both are tired
branches.cn: 两个人争到都累了也没个结果

branches.en: a cabin standing alone beyond the last road
branches.cn: 最后一道路尽头之外孤零零的小屋

branches.en: an unfinished bridge far from the plan
branches.cn: 与图纸相去甚远的半截桥

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English negative na and the question word hwaer; it has no Latin root, and its family is a row of place adverbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的否定词 na 与疑问词 hwær 组成，没有拉丁词根，同族是一整排地点副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: place, as in somewhere or anywhere

definition_zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；细胞核的
definition_en: relating to a nucleus, especially the atomic nucleus or the cell nucleus
core_image: 一个极小的中心，周围绕着一圈电子或一层膜
scene: 这个国家大部分电力来自核电站。The country gets most of its electricity from nuclear power plants.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear 指「核能的」（第 2 个义项：由原子核反应释放能量的）；句意：该国大部分电力来自核电站；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；核武器的；细胞核的；核心家庭的

derivatives.zh: 核；原子核；细胞核
核动力的
无核的
具备核能力的
核工程学（少用）

senses.title: Of the atomic nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 与原子核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear size is measured in femtometres.
senses.exampleCN: 原子核的尺度以飞米计。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun nucleus to atomic physics, where the centre of the atom is the object of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 nucleus 直接接到原子物理上，那里研究的对象就是原子的中心。

senses.title: Nuclear energy
senses.definition: describing energy released by changes in atomic nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 指由原子核变化释放的能量
senses.example: Nuclear power supplies a fifth of the country's electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 核电供应全国五分之一的电力。
senses.why: Because the energy comes from the nucleus rather than from chemical bonds, the adjective names the source of the power.
senses.whyCN: 因为能量来自原子核而不是化学键，这个形容词命名的就是能量的来源。

senses.title: Nuclear weapons
senses.definition: describing weapons whose explosive force comes from nuclear reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指爆炸力来自核反应的武器
senses.example: The treaty limits the number of nuclear warheads.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制核弹头的数量。
senses.why: The same source of energy, released deliberately and instantly, yields a weapon, so the adjective marks the mechanism of the blast.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能量来源若被有意瞬间释放，就成为武器，因此这个形容词标出爆炸的机制。

senses.title: Nuclear physics
senses.definition: relating to the branch of physics that studies nuclei and their reactions
senses.definitionCN: 与研究核及其反应的物理分支有关
senses.example: Nuclear physics grew out of radioactivity research.
senses.exampleCN: 核物理学从放射性研究中发展出来。
senses.why: A discipline named after its object takes the adjective as a fixed modifier, as in nuclear physics or nuclear chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 以研究对象命名的学科会把形容词作为固定修饰语，如 nuclear physics 或 nuclear chemistry。

senses.title: Of the cell nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of a living cell
senses.definitionCN: 与活细胞的细胞核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear DNA is separated from the cytoplasm by a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 核 DNA 由一层膜与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the cell's centre, and compounds such as nuclear envelope keep the two senses distinct by context.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指细胞的中心，nuclear envelope 等复合词靠上下文把两个义项区分开。

senses.title: Nuclear family
senses.definition: describing a household of parents and their dependent children
senses.definitionCN: 指由父母与其未成年子女组成的家庭
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与大家庭。
senses.why: Social science borrowed the image of a small centre with close members, contrasting it with the wider extended family.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借用「小核心加紧密成员」的意象，用来与更宽的扩展家庭相对照。

senses.title: Nuclear medicine
senses.definition: describing medical techniques that use radioactive substances
senses.definitionCN: 指使用放射性物质的医学技术
senses.example: Nuclear medicine scans reveal how an organ is working.
senses.exampleCN: 核医学扫描能显示器官的工作状况。
senses.why: Radioactive tracers are read by their nuclear emissions, so the medical branch is named after the physical process.
senses.whyCN: 放射性示踪剂靠其核辐射被读取，因此这个医学分支按物理过程命名。

senses.title: Nuclear envelope
senses.definition: describing the membrane that surrounds the cell nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指包围细胞核的那层膜
senses.example: The nuclear envelope breaks down during mitosis.
senses.exampleCN: 核膜在有丝分裂过程中解体。
senses.why: An anatomical compound uses the adjective to say which structure the membrane belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学复合词用这个形容词说明这层膜属于哪个结构。

senses.title: Figurative extreme option
senses.definition: in politics, describing an extreme measure reserved as a last resort
senses.definitionCN: 政治语境中指留作最后手段的极端措施
senses.example: Both sides avoided the nuclear option in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在谈判中都避免使用极端手段。
senses.why: The destructive power of nuclear weapons supplies a metaphor for any step that would end the game.
senses.whyCN: 核武器的破坏力为任何「一出手就终结局面」的步骤提供了比喻。

intro.en: Nuclear is the adjective of nucleus, formed with -ar; its history splits between atomic physics and cell biology.
intro.cn: nuclear 是 nucleus 的形容词，由 -ar 构成；它的历史分为原子物理与细胞生物学两条线。

items.en: Nucleus, diminutive of nux 'nut', meant a kernel. English borrowed the noun in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 是 nux「坚果」的指小形式，意为果仁。英语在 17 世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective nuclear is recorded in the 19th century in general senses such as 'relating to a kernel or centre'. The precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 nuclear 在 19 世纪有「与果核或中心有关的」这类一般义。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Robert Brown's nucleus gave biology its own central body, and nuclear later described the structures around it.
items.cn: Robert Brown 的 nucleus 为生物学提供了自己的中心小体，nuclear 后来用于描述它周围的结构。

items.en: Rutherford's model placed nearly all atomic mass in a tiny nucleus, and nuclear physics was born around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福的模型把原子几乎全部质量放进一个极小的核，核物理学约在 1911 至 1912 年诞生。

items.en: The nuclear age fixed the word in public language through weapons and power stations, adding figurative uses such as the nuclear option.
items.cn: 1945 年之后的核时代通过武器与电站把这个词固定进公共语言，并增加了「极端手段」这类比喻用法。

note.en: The first group separates nuclear from the noun and from near-looking words; the second separates its atomic sense from its biological and social senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 nuclear 与名词及形近词分开；第二组把它的原子义与生物、社会义分开。

entries.definition: The central body itself; nuclear is the adjective used in nuclear power, nuclear physics or nuclear envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 指中心小体本身；nuclear 是用于 nuclear power、nuclear physics、nuclear envelope 的形容词。

entries.definition: A structure inside the cell nucleus, not the nucleus; it is a noun and never replaces nuclear as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内的一个结构，不是细胞核本身；它是名词，不能像 nuclear 那样作修饰语。

entries.definition: Used almost only in nucleic acid; it refers to the chemistry of nuclei, not to nuclear energy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎只用于 nucleic acid；它指核的化学，而不是核能。

entries.definition: Relating to atoms as wholes; atomic energy can mean energy from the atom generally, while nuclear pins it to the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个原子有关的；atomic energy 可泛指原子能，而 nuclear 明确限定在原子核。

entries.definition: Describing unstable nuclei that emit radiation; a material can be radioactive without being part of a nuclear reactor.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定的核发出辐射；某种材料可以具有放射性，却与核反应堆无关。

entries.definition: Located at the middle; it is the everyday word for position and never means atomic or cell nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于中间，是表示位置的日常词，从不指原子核或细胞核。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus + -ar: the adjective of the kernel.
normal.cn: nucleus + -ar：果核的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs nucleus, nuclear-powered, nuclear-free and nucleonics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nucleus、nuclear-powered、nuclear-free、nucleonics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: nuclear power, nuclear weapon, nuclear family, nuclear envelope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：核能、核武器、核心家庭、核膜。

normal.en: Context decides whether the nucleus is in an atom or in a cell.
normal.cn: 上下文决定这个核是在原子里还是在细胞里。

normal.en: The nuclear option is a metaphor borrowed from the bomb.
normal.cn: nuclear option 是从核弹借来的比喻。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny sun with a nucleus at the centre and electrons in orbit.
abstract.cn: 原子像一颗微型太阳，原子核在中心，电子在轨道上。

abstract.en: A nuclear family is a small core with a clear boundary, like a nucleus with its membrane.
abstract.cn: 核心家庭像一个有清晰边界的小核心，如同带膜的细胞核。

abstract.en: The nuclear option is the move that ends the game, like a bomb in a board game.
abstract.cn: 极端手段是终结整局棋的那一步，就像棋盘游戏里的炸弹。

examples.en: Nuclear power produces electricity without burning coal.
examples.cn: 核能发电不燃烧煤炭。

examples.en: The nuclear envelope separates the cell's DNA from the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 核膜把细胞的 DNA 与细胞质隔开。

examples.en: The country expanded its nuclear medicine programme.
examples.cn: 该国扩大了核医学项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus（核）+ -ar」→ 跟核有关的 → 原子核的、核能的、细胞核的

root: 拉丁语 nux「坚果」→ nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；加形容词后缀 -ar 构成 nuclear。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide into three families: atomic physics and its power and weapons, cell biology and its envelope, and social or figurative cores such as the nuclear family and the nuclear option.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成三族：原子物理及其能量与武器，细胞生物学及其核膜，以及核心家庭、极端手段这类社会或比喻性的核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny centre with electrons or a membrane wrapped around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个极小的中心，外面绕着一圈电子或一层膜。

branches.en: ATOMIC SCIENCE: the nucleus as an object of study and the discipline built around it.
branches.cn: 原子科学：作为研究对象的原子核，以及围绕它建立的学科。

branches.en: ENERGY AND MEDICINE: power from the nucleus, weapons from the same source, and radioactive tracers.
branches.cn: 能量与医学：来自核的能量，同源的武器，以及放射性示踪剂。

branches.en: CELL BIOLOGY: the nucleus of a living cell and the membrane around it.
branches.cn: 细胞生物学：活细胞的细胞核及其周围的膜。

branches.en: SOCIAL CORE: the small household built around parents and children.
branches.cn: 社会核心：围绕父母与子女建立的小家庭。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the destructive force of the bomb becomes a last-resort political move.
branches.cn: 比喻：核弹的破坏力变成政治上最后才用的手段。

intro.en: Nuclear adds the Latin adjective ending -ar to nucleus; the word then multiplies in compounds.
intro.cn: nuclear 在 nucleus 后加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ar；随后在复合词中大量增殖。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus supply the root; -ar comes from Latin -aris. Compounds such as nuclear-powered and nuclear-free are English formations.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 提供词根；-ar 来自拉丁语 -aris。nuclear-powered、nuclear-free 等复合词是英语构造。

items.example: Nuclear reactions change the identity of atoms.
items.exampleCN: 核反应改变原子的身份。

items.example: The nucleus is the cell's control centre.
items.exampleCN: 细胞核是细胞的控制中心。

items.example: A nuclear-powered submarine can stay under for months.
items.exampleCN: 核动力潜艇能在水下停留数月。
该区域被宣布为无核区。
核工程学涵盖反应堆与同位素。
放射性废料需要长期储存。

definition_en: the central part of a cell or atom, or the core of a group or object
core_image: 一个果核：坚硬的小圆体，所有东西都围着它转
scene: 细胞核里装着它的大部分遗传物质。The nucleus of a cell contains most of its DNA.

senses.title: Cell nucleus
senses.definition: the membrane-bound organelle that contains most of a cell's DNA
senses.definitionCN: 细胞中含有大部分 DNA 的膜结合细胞器
senses.example: The nucleus of a human cell holds twenty-three pairs of chromosomes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类细胞的细胞核里有二十三对染色体。
senses.why: The biological sense was named after the kernel of a nut: a small central body around which the rest is arranged.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义按坚果的果核命名：一个居中的小体，其余部分围绕它安排。

senses.title: Atomic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central core of an atom, made of protons and neutrons
senses.definitionCN: 原子中由质子与中子构成的致密中心
senses.example: The nucleus of carbon-12 contains six protons and six neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-12 的原子核含有六个质子和六个中子。
senses.why: Physics reused the kernel image for the tiny centre of an atom, because almost all its mass sits there.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把果核意象用于原子的微小中心，因为原子几乎全部质量都在那里。

senses.title: Core of a group
senses.definition: the central group of people around whom a larger body forms
senses.definitionCN: 较大群体围绕其形成的核心人群
senses.example: A small nucleus of volunteers kept the project alive.
senses.exampleCN: 一小群志愿者构成的核心让项目维持下去。
senses.why: A group with a hard centre and looser edges matches the kernel image, so the word serves for social structure as well.
senses.whyCN: 一个有坚硬核心与松散边缘的群体符合果核意象，因此这个词也用于社会结构。

senses.title: Central part of an object
senses.definition: the central mass of a comet, crystal or other object
senses.definitionCN: 彗星、晶体或其它物体的中心团块
senses.example: The comet's nucleus is a dirty ball of ice and rock.
senses.exampleCN: 彗核是一个由冰与岩石组成的脏雪球。
senses.why: The word generalises from the kernel to any object's central solid part.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从果核泛化，指任何物体中心那个坚实的部分。

senses.title: Brain nucleus
senses.definition: a cluster of nerve cells in the brain or spinal cord
senses.definitionCN: 脑或脊髓中一簇神经细胞
senses.example: The nucleus accumbens is linked to reward.
senses.exampleCN: 伏隔核与奖赏有关。
senses.why: Anatomists saw clustered cell bodies as kernels inside the nervous tissue, and named them accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家把聚在一起的细胞体看作神经组织里的果核，于是如此命名。

senses.title: Syllable nucleus
senses.definition: the vowel or vowel-like sound that forms the centre of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 构成音节中心的元音或类元音
senses.example: In the word 'cat', the vowel is the syllable nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 在 cat 这个词里，元音就是音节核。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the word for the part every syllable must have at its centre, with consonants around it.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用这个词，指每个音节中心必须具备的成分，辅音围绕它排列。

senses.title: Galactic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central region of a galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 星系中央的致密区域
senses.example: The galactic nucleus glows with billions of old stars.
senses.exampleCN: 星系核因数十亿颗老年恒星而发光。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the kernel image at the largest scale, where mass and light concentrate at the centre.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把果核意象用到最大尺度，那里质量与光都集中在中心。

senses.title: Nucleation centre
senses.definition: a small particle or site where a new phase begins to form
senses.definitionCN: 新相开始形成的小颗粒或位点
senses.example: Dust provides the nuclei on which cloud droplets condense.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃提供了云滴凝结所需的核。
senses.why: A growing crystal or droplet needs a seed at its centre, and the word names that starting point.
senses.whyCN: 生长中的晶体或液滴需要中心的一个种子，这个词就命名那个起点。

senses.title: Nucleus of a collection
senses.definition: the original small set of items around which a larger collection grows
senses.definitionCN: 较大收藏围绕其生长的最初那一小批藏品
senses.example: Six paintings formed the nucleus of the museum's collection.
senses.exampleCN: 六幅画构成了这家博物馆藏品的核心。
senses.why: The kernel image extends to collections: a small hard core of founding items attracts more around it.
senses.whyCN: 果核意象延伸到收藏：一小批创始藏品构成坚硬的核心，吸引更多东西围绕它聚集。

intro.en: Nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel; science then applied the little central body to cells, atoms, brains and galaxies.
intro.cn: nucleus 在拉丁语里指坚果的果核；科学随后把这个居中的小体用于细胞、原子、脑与星系。

items.en: Latin nux, with the stem nuc-, meant a nut. Its diminutive nucleus meant the small kernel inside a shell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nux（词干 nuc-）指坚果。其指小形式 nucleus 指壳内的小果仁。

items.en: Nucleus kept the physical sense of a kernel, and by extension any hard central part. English borrowed it in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 保留了果仁的具体意义，并引申指任何坚硬的中心部分。英语在 17 世纪借入。

items.en: Robert Brown described a small body inside plant cells and called it the nucleus in 1831, a term generally credited to him.
items.cn: Robert Brown 在 1831 年描述植物细胞内的一个小体并称之为 nucleus，这一术语一般认为出自他。

items.en: After Rutherford's scattering experiments, the dense centre of the atom was called the nucleus. The date is approximate, around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福散射实验之后，原子的致密中心被称为 nucleus。年代约为 1911 至 1912 年。

items.en: The word spread to astronomy, neuroanatomy and linguistics, always keeping the shape of a centre with surrounding parts.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到天文学、神经解剖学与语言学，始终保留「中心加周围部分」的形状。

note.en: The first group separates nucleus from the adjective and from the smaller body inside it; the second separates it from general words for a centre.
note.cn: 第一组把 nucleus 与它的形容词以及它内部更小的结构分开；第二组把它与泛指的「中心」词分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of a nucleus'; it is used in nuclear physics and nuclear envelope, while nucleus is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「核的」，用于核物理与核膜等；nucleus 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A small structure within the cell nucleus where ribosomes are assembled; it is not the nucleus itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内组装核糖体的小结构，不是细胞核本身。

entries.definition: The building block of DNA and RNA; it shares the nuc- root through the idea of a core, but names a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指 DNA 与 RNA 的构件；它通过「核心」的观念共享 nuc- 词根，但指的是分子。

entries.definition: The central part of anything, often of an apple or the earth; it is the everyday synonym of nucleus outside science.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何事物的中心部分，常见于苹果核或地核；是 nucleus 在科学之外的日常同义词。

entries.definition: The middle point or area of a space; it describes position, not a distinct body with surrounding parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间的中心点或区域，描述位置，而不是一个带周围部分的独立小体。

entries.definition: The edible part inside a nut, and the literal sense behind nucleus; it is also used figuratively for the essence of a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚果内的可食部分，是 nucleus 背后的字面义；也比喻事情的要点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel: the hard thing in the middle.
normal.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语的「果仁」：中间那个硬东西。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear, nucleolus, nucleated, enucleate and nucleation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nuclear、nucleolus、nucleated、enucleate、nucleation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cell nucleus, atomic nucleus, comet nucleus, syllable nucleus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞核、原子核、彗核、音节核。

normal.en: The plural is nuclei, not nucleuses, in scientific writing.
normal.cn: 科学写作中复数用 nuclei，而不用 nucleuses。

normal.en: Every use keeps the same picture: a centre with a surrounding body.
normal.cn: 每个用法都保留同一幅图：一个中心加一个围绕它的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a peach: the stone is the nucleus, the flesh is everything that surrounds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只桃子：桃核是 nucleus，果肉是围绕它的一切。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny solar system with the nucleus as its sun.
abstract.cn: 原子像一个微型太阳系，原子核就是它的太阳。

abstract.en: A nucleus of volunteers is a seed crystal around which a project forms.
abstract.cn: 志愿者的核心就是一颗种子晶体，项目围绕它生长。

examples.en: The nucleus stores the cell's chromosomes and controls gene expression.
examples.cn: 细胞核储存细胞的染色体并控制基因表达。

examples.en: Protons and neutrons occupy the atomic nucleus.
examples.cn: 质子与中子占据原子核。

examples.en: A small nucleus of supporters organised the campaign.
examples.cn: 一小群支持者构成的核心组织了这场运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus 就是果核」→ 中间那个核 → 细胞核、原子核、核心

root: 拉丁语 nux（坚果，词干 nuc-）→ 指小形式 nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；细胞核义始于 1831 年 Robert Brown，原子核义约始于 1911 年。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one shape: a compact centre surrounded by a larger body. The kernel becomes a cell organelle, an atomic core, a group of people, a comet's heart, a brain cluster, a syllable's vowel, a galactic centre, a seed crystal, and finally the founding core of a collection.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一种形状：一个紧凑的中心，被更大的整体包围。果仁先后变成细胞器、原子核心、人群核心、彗星中心、脑内细胞簇、音节元音、星系中心、成核种子，最后成为一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard kernel at the centre, with everything else arranged around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：中央一颗坚硬的果核，其余一切都围着它安排。

branches.en: THE TWO SCIENTIFIC CENTRES: the organelle that holds DNA, and the dense core of the atom.
branches.cn: 两个科学中心：保存 DNA 的细胞器，以及原子的致密核心。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND PHYSICAL CORES: a founding group, and the solid centre of a comet or crystal.
branches.cn: 社会与物理核心：一个创始群体，以及彗星或晶体的坚实中心。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND ASTRONOMY: clustered nerve cells, and the centre of a galaxy.
branches.cn: 解剖与天文：聚成一团的神经细胞，以及星系的中心。

branches.en: LINGUISTICS: the vowel at the centre of a syllable.
branches.cn: 语言学：音节中心的元音。

branches.en: SEED AND SOURCE: the site where growth starts, and the founding core of a collection.
branches.cn: 种子与本源：生长开始的位点，以及一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

intro.en: Nucleus is a Latin diminutive with no prefix; its family is built with -ar, -olus and -ation.
intro.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语指小词，不带前缀；其词族由 -ar、-olus、-ation 等构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and its diminutive nucleus supply the root. The adjective nuclear adds -ar; nucleolus is a further diminutive; nucleation adds -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 及其指小形式 nucleus 提供词根。形容词 nuclear 加 -ar；nucleolus 是再一层指小；nucleation 加 -ation。

definition_zh: 麻烦事；令人讨厌的事；讨厌的人；妨害公众的行为
definition_en: something or someone that annoys people or causes trouble; in law, an activity that harms the public
core_image: 一只蚊子贴着耳边打转，整晚的睡意被它一点点搅散
scene: 盛夏的夜里，窗纱破了一个小洞，耳边总有一阵嗡嗡声挥之不去。The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人讨厌的事、麻烦」（第 1 个义项：带来困扰的事物）；句意为那持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。破窗纱与蚊子正是这种小烦扰的来源。

由 nuisance 与 tax 合成的复合词，指琐碎而扰人的小额税
由 nuisance 加 -free 构成，义为「没有烦扰的」

senses.title: Something that annoys or troubles
senses.definition: a thing, situation or event that annoys people or causes them trouble
senses.definitionCN: 让人心烦或给人添麻烦的事物、情况或事件
senses.example: The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
senses.exampleCN: 持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。
senses.why: Old French nuisance meant harm and annoyance, from a verb for hurting, so the word begins as the discomfort itself rather than the thing causing it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 nuisance 意为「损害、烦扰」，源自表示「伤害」的动词，所以这个词一开始指的就是那份不舒服，而不是造成它的东西。

senses.title: A person who annoys others
senses.titleCN: 讨厌的人；讨人嫌的家伙
senses.definition: a person whose behaviour annoys other people
senses.definitionCN: 行为让别人厌烦的人
senses.example: He made a nuisance of himself at the party by shouting all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上整晚大喊大叫，很讨人嫌。
senses.why: Once annoyance has a name, that name easily shifts from the feeling to the person who reliably produces it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「烦扰」有了名字，这个名字很容易从那种感受转到总能制造出这种感受的人身上。

senses.title: A legal harm to the public
senses.definition: in law, an activity or condition that interferes with the public comfort or safety
senses.definitionCN: 法律上干扰公众安宁或安全的行为或状态
senses.example: The factory was sued for creating a public nuisance with its smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因排放烟雾构成妨害公众而被起诉。
senses.why: Because the earliest sense was plain harm, the law kept the word for conduct that harms a whole neighbourhood, not just one person.
senses.whyCN: 因为最早的意思就是「损害」，法律便保留这个词，用来指伤害整个街区而不只是某个人的行为。

intro.en: Nuisance came through French from a Latin verb for harming, and it still carries that original sting.
intro.cn: nuisance 经法语来自一个表示「伤害」的拉丁动词，至今还带着最初的那根刺。

items.en: Nocere meant to hurt or harm, and it is the root behind noxious and innocent as well.
items.cn: nocere 意为伤害、损害，也是 noxious 与 innocent 的共同词根。

items.en: Medieval Latin nocumentum named a harm or an injury done to someone.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 nocumentum 指对他人造成的损害或伤害。

items.en: Old French shortened the family to nuire, the verb for harming or annoying.
items.cn: 古法语把这族词简化为 nuire，即「伤害、烦扰」的动词。

items.en: The noun nuisance meant harm, annoyance and trouble in Old French.
items.cn: 名词 nuisance 在古法语中意为损害、烦扰与麻烦。

items.en: English borrowed it for annoyance of any kind and later gave it a precise legal sense.
items.cn: 英语借来泛指各种烦扰，后来又赋予它精确的法律含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root for harm; the near-meaning group collects words for annoyance and for the people who cause it.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「伤害」拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示烦扰以及制造烦扰者的词。

entries.definition: Harmful to health, or strongly unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 对健康有害的，或气味强烈令人不快的。

entries.definition: Harmless and unlikely to upset anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 无害的，不太会惹人不安的。

entries.definition: Not guilty of doing anything wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 没有做错事的；无罪的。

entries.definition: Harmful or guilty; now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的或有罪的；现已罕见。

entries.definition: The feeling of being irritated, or something that irritates.
entries.definitionCN: 被惹恼的感受，或惹人恼的事物。

entries.definition: Trouble or effort that is annoying.
entries.definitionCN: 令人烦的麻烦或费劲。

entries.definition: A person or thing that keeps annoying others.
entries.definitionCN: 不断烦扰他人的人或物。

entries.definition: Bothering trouble or a series of small problems.
entries.definitionCN: 恼人的麻烦或一连串小问题。

normalIntro.en: The bone of the word is the Latin verb nocere, to harm, which is why nuisance grew from harm into annoyance and then into a legal wrong.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的骨头是拉丁语动词 nocere（伤害），所以 nuisance 从「损害」长成「烦扰」，再被法律固定成一种侵害。

normal.en: Nuisance and noxious share the Latin verb nocere, which means to harm.
normal.cn: nuisance 与 noxious 共用拉丁动词 nocere，意为伤害。

normal.en: The French noun moved from harm to mere annoyance, which is why the English word sounds milder than its root.
normal.cn: 法语名词从「损害」滑向「烦扰」，所以英语这个词听起来比它的词根温和。

normal.en: Innocent and innocuous add a negative prefix to the same root and turn harmful into harmless.
normal.cn: innocent 与 innocuous 在同一词根前加否定前缀，把「有害」变成「无害」。

normal.en: Public nuisance keeps the legal sense, naming conduct that harms a whole community.
normal.cn: public nuisance 保留法律义，指伤害整个社区的行为。

normal.en: Make a nuisance of oneself is the fixed phrase for a person who keeps bothering others.
normal.cn: make a nuisance of oneself 是固定说法，指不断给别人添烦的人。

abstract.en: A word for harm that softened into annoyance shows how often law and daily speech borrow from each other.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「伤害」的词软化成「烦扰」，正说明法律与日常语言常常互相借用。

abstract.en: Nuisance is small in scale but large in effect: one mosquito can cancel a whole night.
abstract.cn: nuisance 的规模很小，效果却很大：一只蚊子就能毁掉一整夜。

abstract.en: The same root that names poison also names harmlessness, depending on the prefix it wears.
abstract.cn: 给毒物命名的那个词根，也能给无害命名，全看它披着哪块前缀。

examples.en: The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
examples.cn: 持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。

examples.en: He made a nuisance of himself at the party by shouting all evening.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上整晚大喊大叫，很讨人嫌。

examples.en: The factory was sued for creating a public nuisance with its smoke.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因排放烟雾构成妨害公众而被起诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛搔死」——牛被蚊子搔得受不了，真是件麻烦事；记住 nuisance 是烦扰。

root: 拉丁语 nocere（伤害）→ 中世纪拉丁语 nocumentum（损害）→ 古法语 nuire（伤害）→ 古法语 nuisance（烦扰）→ 英语 nuisance（讨厌的事、妨害公众）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is causing annoyance; the senses run from an irritating thing to an irritating person and finally to a legal harm to the public.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造成烦扰」；义项先指烦人的事物，再转到制造烦扰的人，最后落到法律上的妨害公众。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mosquito circling a sleeping ear and undoing a whole night of rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蚊子贴着睡觉的耳边打转，把整夜的休息一点点搅散。

branches.en: a mosquito circling one ear in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗里绕着耳边飞的蚊子

branches.en: a phone buzzing with sales calls at midnight
branches.cn: 半夜被推销电话震得响个不停的手机

branches.en: a neighbour who shouts every evening
branches.cn: 每晚都大喊大叫的邻居

branches.en: a guest who will not stop complaining
branches.cn: 抱怨个不停的客人

branches.en: smoke from a factory drifting over a whole street
branches.cn: 工厂的烟飘过整条街

intro.en: The word stands on a Latin root for harm and travels through a Latin noun, a French verb and a French noun before English gives it a legal sense.
intro.cn: 这个词立在一个表示「伤害」的拉丁词根上，经拉丁名词、法语动词与法语名词一路传下来，再由英语给它添上法律义。

latinIntro.en: Latin nocere and its noun nocumentum supply the core idea of harm, and the related adjective noxius survives inside the English word noxious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nocere 及其名词 nocumentum 提供了「伤害」这一核心，同族的形容词 noxius 还留在英语的 noxious 里。
